key_insight: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) produce a small number of high-norm "outlier" tokens (in both encoder and denoiser) that attract disproportionate attention while carrying little local information; identifying and taming these tokens leads to more reliable, higher-quality image generation.
problem_solved: Outlier tokens in ViT-based diffusion pipelines skew attention and conditioning, degrading generation fidelity and robustness in Representation Autoencoder (RAE)-DiT image models.
method: Empirical diagnosis: detect and characterize high-norm outlier tokens in pretrained ViT encoders and DiT denoisers (token-norm distributions, attention patterns).
Impact analysis: measure how outlier tokens concentrate attention and affect denoising and reconstructed image quality.
Mitigation strategies: apply targeted interventions (e.g., token norm regularization / clipping, attention reweighting or selective pruning, and light fine-tuning) to reduce outlier influence.
impact: Taming outlier tokens makes DiT-based image generation more stable and faithful to local image content, improving sample quality and reliability for practitioners building diffusion + transformer pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: RAE → ViT encoder → DiT denoiser with outlier tokens highlighted to show where the problem arises.
Token-norm histogram: long-tail distribution highlighting a few high-norm outliers vs majority of normal tokens.
Attention heatmaps: before vs after mitigation to show attention concentration on outliers being reduced.
Performance bar chart: qualitative/quantitative metrics (e.g., fidelity, stability) compared pre/post mitigation.
paper_title: Taming Outlier Tokens in Diffusion Transformers
paper_authors: Xiaoyu Wu, Yifei Wang, Tsu-Jui Fu, Liang-Chieh Chen, Zhe Gan
